sections.html: Telmatherina bonti (most likely; identification of Telmatherina species is highly complex) grows to about 8 cm. It is a very peaceful, lively and easy-to-keep fish that should always be kept in a school.
The Malili Lake System on Sulawesi (formerly Celebes) consists of five lakes, three large and two small: Matano, Towuti, Mahalona, Lontoa and Masapi. The species is endemic to this area.
The water in the Malili Lakes is always relatively warm (approx. 28°C) and its pH is always above 8. Both conditions should be replicated in the aquarium.
They will eat any dry or frozen food.

In the aquarium, T. bonti are very peaceful and lively fish. They captivate with their lively nature and constant courtship displays. It never gets boring to watch a school of these fish, and with this species it should always be a school.

Like many Malilian silversides, this species is polychromatic: both males and females occur in various colour variations. In T. bonti there are yellow, white and yellow-white individuals. In the wild they occur in a colourful mix and also interbreed, so they are by no means distinct breeds or subspecies. The purpose of this polychromatism is unknown.
Spawning takes place among fine-leaved plants. The fish are continuous spawners.

Lexicon: Telmatherina comes from the ancient Greek "telma", meaning "swamp"; Atherina is another genus of silverside. bonti is named after the local name of the species, "bonti-bonti", at Lake Towuti.
